questions.knowledgeNote: Even x even = even: (-x)sin(-x) = (-x)(-sinx) = x sinx, and cos(-x) = cosx.
questions.question: Q1(a). Examine whether f(x) = x sin x + cos x is even, odd or neither.
questions.solution: f(-x) = (-x)sin(-x) + cos(-x) = (-x)(-sin x) + cos x = x sin x + cos x = f(x). Even. Matches the printed Answers key (p129): 'a) Even'.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.3 Ex 3.1 Q1(a); book p128 = PDF p155 (statement via 200-dpi image read); matches printed key

questions.knowledgeNote: Even + odd (both present, neither zero) can never be purely even or purely odd.
questions.question: Q1(b). Examine whether f(x) = 5x^2 + sin x is even, odd or neither.
questions.solution: f(-x) = 5x^2 - sin x. This equals neither f(x) (= 5x^2 + sin x) nor -f(x) (= -5x^2 - sin x) (e.g. at x = pi/2: f = 5pi^2/4+1 vs f(-pi/2) = 5pi^2/4-1). Neither. Matches the printed Answers key: 'b) Neither'.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.3 Ex 3.1 Q1(b); book p128 = PDF p155; matches printed key

questions.knowledgeNote: x appears only as x^2, so -x changes nothing: automatically even.
questions.question: Q1(c). Examine whether f(x) = sqrt(1+x^2) - sqrt(1-x^2) is even, odd or neither.
questions.solution: f(-x) = sqrt(1+(-x)^2) - sqrt(1-(-x)^2) = sqrt(1+x^2) - sqrt(1-x^2) = f(x). Even. Matches the printed Answers key: 'c) Even'. (The scan merges Q1(d)'s fraction bar into this line; (c) is the numerator alone - confirmed by 200-dpi image read.)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.3 Ex 3.1 Q1(c); book p128 = PDF p155 (image read); matches printed key

questions.knowledgeNote: sqrt(1-x) and sqrt(1+x) swap under x -> -x, flipping the overall sign.
questions.question: Q1(d). Examine whether f(x) = sqrt(1+x) - sqrt(1-x) (domain [-1,1]) is even, odd or neither.
questions.solution: f(-x) = sqrt(1-x) - sqrt(1+x) = -f(x). Odd. (The printed key's d/e/f letters are OCR-garbled; the parity follows decisively from substitution. Domain [-1,1] is symmetric, so the test is valid.)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.3 Ex 3.1 Q1(d); book p128 = PDF p155 (image read); parity by substitution

questions.knowledgeNote: a^x and a^(-x) swap under x -> -x: their difference negates.
questions.question: Q1(e). Examine whether f(x) = 10^x - 10^(-x) is even, odd or neither.
questions.solution: f(-x) = 10^(-x) - 10^x = -f(x). Odd. (Key letters garbled in scan; substitution is decisive.)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.3 Ex 3.1 Q1(e); book p128 = PDF p155 (image read); parity by substitution

questions.knowledgeNote: tanh(-x) = -tanh x: numerator and denominator swap roles up to a sign.
questions.question: Q1(f). Examine whether f(x) = (e^x - e^(-x))/(e^x + e^(-x)) is even, odd or neither.
questions.solution: f(-x) = (e^(-x) - e^x)/(e^(-x) + e^x) = -(e^x - e^(-x))/(e^x + e^(-x)) = -f(x). Odd (this is tanh x). (Key letters garbled in scan; substitution is decisive.)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.3 Ex 3.1 Q1(f); book p128 = PDF p155 (image read); parity by substitution

questions.knowledgeNote: Only even powers: f(-x) = f(x) term by term - mirror symmetry in the y-axis.
questions.question: Q2(a). Test the symmetricity of f(x) = x^4 + 3x^2 + 1.
questions.solution: f(-x) = x^4 + 3x^2 + 1 = f(x): symmetric about the y-axis. Matches the printed Answers key: 'a) Symmetric about y-axis'.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.3 Ex 3.1 Q2(a); book p128 = PDF p155; matches printed key

questions.knowledgeNote: cos is even and the window [-pi/2, pi/2] is symmetric about 0, so the mirror symmetry survives the restriction.
questions.question: Q2(b). Test the symmetricity of f(x) = cos x (-pi/2 <= x <= pi/2).
questions.solution: cos(-x) = cos x on the symmetric domain: symmetric about the y-axis. Matches the printed Answers key: 'b) Symmetric about y-axis'.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.3 Ex 3.1 Q2(b); book p128 = PDF p155 (image read); matches printed key

questions.knowledgeNote: Odd powers only: every term flips sign - half-turn symmetry about the origin.
questions.question: Q2(c). Test the symmetricity of f(x) = x^3 - x.
questions.solution: f(-x) = -x^3 + x = -f(x): symmetric about the origin. Matches the printed Answers key: 'c) Symmetric about origin'.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.3 Ex 3.1 Q2(c); book p128 = PDF p155; matches printed key

questions.knowledgeNote: x appears only as x^2 under the root: f(-x) = f(x) on the symmetric domain [-2,2].
questions.question: Q2(d). Test the symmetricity of f(x) = sqrt(4-x^2).
questions.solution: f(-x) = sqrt(4-x^2) = f(x): symmetric about the y-axis (upper half of the circle x^2+y^2 = 4). Matches the printed Answers key: 'd) Symmetric about y-axis'.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.3 Ex 3.1 Q2(d); book p128 = PDF p155 (image read); matches printed key

questions.knowledgeNote: sin(2(x+pi)) = sin(2x+2pi) = sin 2x: doubling the speed halves the period.
questions.question: Q3(a). Test the periodicity of f(x) = sin 2x and find its period.
questions.solution: f(x+pi) = sin(2x+2pi) = sin 2x = f(x), and no smaller positive shift works (2x must advance by a full 2pi). Periodic with period pi. Matches the printed Answers key: 'a) Periodic, pi'.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.3 Ex 3.1 Q3(a); book p128 = PDF p155; matches printed key

questions.knowledgeNote: cos(u+2pi) = cos u: set u = pi.x and solve pi(x+T) = pi.x+2pi for T.
questions.question: Q3(b). Test the periodicity of f(x) = cos(pi x) and find its period.
questions.solution: f(x+2) = cos(pi x + 2pi) = cos(pi x) = f(x), and 2 is minimal (needs pi.T = 2pi). Periodic with period 2. Matches the printed Answers key: 'b) Periodic, 2'. (The bare '2' in the key is complete - not truncated.)
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.3 Ex 3.1 Q3(b); book p128 = PDF p155 (image read: cos pi x); matches printed key

questions.knowledgeNote: tan repeats every pi in its argument: (x+T)/4 = x/4+pi gives T = 4pi.
questions.question: Q3(c). Test the periodicity of f(x) = tan(x/4) and find its period.
questions.solution: f(x+4pi) = tan(x/4 + pi) = tan(x/4) = f(x), minimal since tan's own period is pi. Periodic with period 4pi. Matches the printed Answers key: 'c) Periodic, 4pi'.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.3 Ex 3.1 Q3(c); book p128 = PDF p155 (image read: tan x/4); matches printed key

questions.knowledgeNote: a > 0 stretches/compresses the wave: the argument must still advance by 2pi, so T = 2pi/a.
questions.question: Q3(d). Test the periodicity of f(x) = sin(ax+b) (a > 0) and find its period.
questions.solution: f(x+T) = sin(a(x+T)+b) = sin(ax+b+aT); this equals sin(ax+b) for all x iff aT = 2pi, i.e. T = 2pi/a (minimal positive). Periodic with period 2pi/a. NOTE: the key OCR reads 'd) Periodic, 2pi' - the '/a' was very likely dropped in print/OCR; 2pi/a is the correct general form (it gives 2pi only for a = 1).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.3 Ex 3.1 Q3(d); book p128 = PDF p155 (image read: sin(ax+b), a > 0); '/a' flagged vs key OCR

questions.knowledgeNote: sin and cos share period 2pi, so their sum cannot repeat any faster.
questions.question: Q3(e). Test the periodicity of f(x) = sin x + cos x and find its period.
questions.solution: f(x) = sqrt(2) sin(x+pi/4), so f(x+2pi) = f(x); any smaller shift breaks at least one of sin/cos. Periodic with period 2pi. Matches the printed Answers key: 'e) Periodic, 2pi'.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.3 Ex 3.1 Q3(e); book p128 = PDF p155; matches printed key

questions.knowledgeNote: Positive slope preserves order: x1 > x2 implies 5x1 > 5x2.
questions.question: Q4(a). Prove that f(x) = 3 + 5x is increasing for all x in R.
questions.solution: Let x1 > x2. Then 5x1 > 5x2 (multiplying by positive 5), so 3+5x1 > 3+5x2, i.e. f(x1) > f(x2). Hence f is (strictly) increasing on R.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.3 Ex 3.1 Q4(a); book p128 = PDF p155

questions.knowledgeNote: Negative slope reverses order: multiplying by -4 flips the inequality.
questions.question: Q4(b). Prove that f(x) = 5 - 4x is decreasing for all x in R.
questions.solution: Let x1 > x2. Then -4x1 < -4x2 (multiplying by negative -4 flips), so 5-4x1 < 5-4x2, i.e. f(x1) < f(x2). Hence f is (strictly) decreasing on R.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.3 Ex 3.1 Q4(b); book p128 = PDF p155

questions.knowledgeNote: Straight line: two intercepts fix it - (2/3,0) on the x-axis, (0,-2) on the y-axis.
questions.question: Q5(a). Draw the graph of y = 3x - 2.
questions.solution: Intercepts: y = 0 gives x = 2/3; x = 0 gives y = -2. Join (2/3,0) and (0,-2) with a straight line (slope 3 > 0, rising). Cross-checked against the printed figure (book p130 = PDF p157): intercepts (2/3,0), (0,-2) labelled.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.3 Ex 3.1 Q5(a); book p128 = PDF p155 (image read); figure p130 verified

questions.knowledgeNote: Complete the square: (x+1)^2+2 >= 2 - vertex (-1,2), never touches the x-axis.
questions.question: Q5(b). Draw the graph of y = x^2 + 2x + 3.
questions.solution: y = (x+1)^2 + 2: vertex (-1,2) (minimum, since leading coefficient positive); y-intercept (0,3); discriminant 4-12 < 0 so no x-intercepts; symmetric about x = -1. Cross-checked against the printed figure (p130): vertex (-1,2) and (0,3) labelled.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.3 Ex 3.1 Q5(b); book p128 = PDF p155 (image read); figure p130 verified

questions.knowledgeNote: Downward parabola: roots at x = 1 and x = 3 (factor -(x-1)(x-3)), peak midway at (2,1).
questions.question: Q5(c). Draw the graph of y = -x^2 + 4x - 3.
questions.solution: y = -(x-1)(x-3): x-intercepts (1,0),(3,0); vertex at x = 2, y = 1 (maximum); y-intercept (0,-3); symmetric about x = 2. Cross-checked against the printed figure (p130): (1,0),(3,0) and vertex (2,1) labelled.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.3 Ex 3.1 Q5(c); book p128 = PDF p155 (image read); figure p130 verified

questions.knowledgeNote: Rectangular hyperbola: axes are the asymptotes - the curve lives in quadrants I and III, never touching x = 0 or y = 0.
questions.question: Q5(d). Draw the graph of y = 1/x.
questions.solution: Domain x != 0; vertical asymptote x = 0, horizontal asymptote y = 0; passes through (1,1),(-1,-1); quadrant I branch decreasing from +inf to 0, quadrant III branch decreasing from 0 to -inf; symmetric about the origin (odd). Standard figure (p130 set).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.3 Ex 3.1 Q5(d); book p128 = PDF p155 (image read: y = 1/x)

questions.knowledgeNote: Shift 1/x right by 3: the vertical asymptote moves to x = 3, point (4,1) anchors the right branch.
questions.question: Q5(e). Draw the graph of y = 1/(x-3).
questions.solution: Domain x != 3; vertical asymptote x = 3, horizontal asymptote y = 0; passes through (4,1),(2,-1); same two-branch shape as 1/x translated 3 units right. Standard figure (p130 set).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.3 Ex 3.1 Q5(e); book p128 = PDF p155 (image read: y = 1/(x-3))

questions.knowledgeNote: Factor first: (x^2-1)/(x-1) = x+1 for x != 1 - a straight line with a single hole at (1,2).
questions.question: Q5(f). Draw the graph of y = (x^2-1)/(x-1).
questions.solution: For x != 1, y = (x-1)(x+1)/(x-1) = x+1: the line through (0,1) with slope 1, EXCEPT the hole at x = 1, i.e. missing point (1,2) (limit value). Mark (1,2) with an open circle. Standard figure (p130-131 set).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.3 Ex 3.1 Q5(f); book p128 = PDF p155 (image read); hole at (1,2) stressed

questions.knowledgeNote: Factored cubic: roots 1,2,3 read straight off; y-intercept (-1)(-2)(-3) = -6; positive leading coefficient: down-left to up-right.
questions.question: Q5(g). Draw the graph of f(x) = (x-1)(x-2)(x-3).
questions.solution: x-intercepts (1,0),(2,0),(3,0); y-intercept (0,-6); as x -> -inf, f -> -inf; as x -> +inf, f -> +inf; one local max in (1,2), one local min in (2,3). Cross-checked against the printed figure (p130-131): (2,0) and (0,-6) labelled.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.3 Ex 3.1 Q5(g); book p128 = PDF p155 (image read); figure labels (2,0),(0,-6) verified

questions.knowledgeNote: Double root at 0: the curve touches the x-axis and turns back, then crosses at x = 2.
questions.question: Q5(h). Draw the graph of y = x^2(x-2).
questions.solution: x-intercepts: 0 (double - touches, does not cross) and 2 (simple - crosses); y-intercept (0,0); as x -> -inf, y -> -inf; as x -> +inf, y -> +inf; falls from 0 to a local min in (0,2), then rises through (2,0). Standard figure (p131 set).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.3 Ex 3.1 Q5(h); book p128 = PDF p155 (image read)

questions.knowledgeNote: Base 2, flipped exponent: mirror of 2^x in the y-axis - (1,1/2) is the anchor.
questions.question: Q6(a). Draw the graph of y = 2^(-x).
questions.solution: = (1/2)^x: passes through (0,1),(1,1/2),(-1,2); horizontal asymptote y = 0 (as x -> +inf); strictly decreasing; mirror of y = 2^x. Cross-checked against the printed figure (p131): (0,1),(1,1/2) labelled.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.3 Ex 3.1 Q6(a); book p129 = PDF p156 (image read: 2^(-x)); figure p131 verified

questions.knowledgeNote: Classic growth curve through (0,1) and (1,3), hugging y = 0 on the left.
questions.question: Q6(b). Draw the graph of y = 3^x.
questions.solution: Passes through (0,1),(1,3),(-1,1/3); horizontal asymptote y = 0 as x -> -inf; strictly increasing. Cross-checked against the printed figure (p131): (0,1) labelled.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.3 Ex 3.1 Q6(b); book p129 = PDF p156 (image read: 3^x); figure p131 verified

questions.knowledgeNote: Base 1/3 < 1: decay curve, mirror of 3^x - (1,1/3) is the anchor.
questions.question: Q6(c). Draw the graph of y = (1/3)^x.
questions.solution: Passes through (0,1),(1,1/3),(-1,3); horizontal asymptote y = 0 as x -> +inf; strictly decreasing. Cross-checked against the printed figure (p131): (0,1),(1,1/3) labelled.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.3 Ex 3.1 Q6(c); book p129 = PDF p156 (image read); figure p131 verified

questions.knowledgeNote: Inverse of 3^x: swap the axes - (1,0) and (3,1) anchor it, x = 0 is the asymptote.
questions.question: Q6(d). Draw the graph of y = log_3 x.
questions.solution: Domain x > 0; vertical asymptote x = 0; passes through (1,0),(3,1); strictly increasing; reflection of y = 3^x in y = x. Cross-checked against the printed figure (p131): (1,0),(3,1) labelled.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.3 Ex 3.1 Q6(d); book p129 = PDF p156 (image read: log_3 x); figure p131 verified

questions.knowledgeNote: Common log: same shape as log_3 x, stretched - (10,1) is the anchor.
questions.question: Q6(e). Draw the graph of y = log_10 x.
questions.solution: Domain x > 0; vertical asymptote x = 0; passes through (1,0),(10,1); strictly increasing. Cross-checked against the printed figure (p131): (1,0),(10,1) labelled.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.3 Ex 3.1 Q6(e); book p129 = PDF p156 (image read); figure p131 verified

questions.knowledgeNote: One full wave on [0,2pi]: start (0,1), zeros at pi/2 and 3pi/2, trough (pi,-1), end (2pi,1).
questions.question: Q6(f). Draw the graph of y = cos x (0 <= x <= 2pi).
questions.solution: Key points: (0,1),(pi/2,0),(pi,-1),(3pi/2,0),(2pi,1); amplitude 1, period 2pi; symmetric about x = pi on this window. Cross-checked against the printed figure (p131): (0,1),(2pi,1) and zeros labelled.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.3 Ex 3.1 Q6(f); book p129 = PDF p156 (image read); figure p131 verified

questions.knowledgeNote: Symmetric wave through the origin: zeros at -pi, 0, pi; peak (pi/2,1), trough (-pi/2,-1).
questions.question: Q6(g). Draw the graph of y = sin x (-pi <= x <= pi).
questions.solution: Key points: (-pi,0),(-pi/2,-1),(0,0),(pi/2,1),(pi,0); amplitude 1; odd symmetry about the origin. Cross-checked against the printed figure (p131): (0,0),(pi,0),(pi/2,0-label set) consistent.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.3 Ex 3.1 Q6(g); book p129 = PDF p156 (image read); figure p131 verified

questions.knowledgeNote: Branches between vertical asymptotes at -pi/2 and pi/2: rises from -inf to +inf through (0,0).
questions.question: Q6(h). Draw the graph of y = tan x (-pi < x < pi).
questions.solution: Vertical asymptotes x = +-pi/2 (also x = +-pi at the window edge); passes through (0,0),(pi/4,1),(-pi/4,-1); strictly increasing on each branch (-pi/2,pi/2); odd symmetry. (Endpoints -pi, pi excluded: tan undefined at +-pi/2 inside.) Standard figure (p131-132 set).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.3 Ex 3.1 Q6(h); book p129 = PDF p156 (image read)

questions.knowledgeNote: y = (x-2)^2 is y = x^2 shifted 2 right: vertex moves (0,0) -> (2,0).
questions.question: Q7(a)(i). Sketch y = x^2 and hence draw y = (x-2)^2.
questions.solution: Base: parabola vertex (0,0), through (1,1),(-1,1). Replace x by x-2: every point shifts 2 right: vertex (2,0), through (3,1),(1,1). Cross-checked against the printed figure (p132): (2,0) labelled.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.3 Ex 3.1 Q7(a)(i); book p129 = PDF p156 (image read); figure p132 verified

questions.knowledgeNote: x^2-6x+5 = (x-3)^2-4: shift right 3, down 4 - roots factor as (x-1)(x-5).
questions.question: Q7(a)(ii). Using y = x^2, draw y = x^2 - 6x + 5.
questions.solution: y = (x-3)^2 - 4: vertex (3,-4); x-intercepts from (x-1)(x-5): (1,0),(5,0); y-intercept (0,5). I.e. y = x^2 shifted 3 right and 4 down. Cross-checked against the printed figure (p132): (1,0),(5,0) labelled.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.3 Ex 3.1 Q7(a)(ii); book p129 = PDF p156 (image read); figure p132 verified

questions.knowledgeNote: x -> -x mirrors left-right: the vertex jumps from (1,-4) to (-1,-4), roots from {3,-1}... check: x^2-2x-3 = (x-3)(x+1) roots 3,-1; mirrored roots -3,1 = x^2+2x-3.
questions.question: Q7(b). Sketch y = x^2 - 2x - 3 and hence draw y = x^2 + 2x - 3.
questions.solution: Base: vertex (1,-4) (x = 1), roots (3,0),(-1,0), y-intercept (0,-3). Replace x by -x (y-axis reflection): vertex (-1,-4), roots (-3,0),(1,0), same y-intercept (0,-3): y = x^2+2x-3. Cross-checked against the printed figure (p132): (1,-4) and (-1,-4) labelled.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.3 Ex 3.1 Q7(b); book p129 = PDF p156 (image read); figure p132 verified

questions.knowledgeNote: Right 1, down 2: the inflection point (0,0) of x^3 moves to (1,-2).
questions.question: Q7(c). Sketch y = x^3 and hence draw y = (x-1)^3 - 2.
questions.solution: Base: cubic through (-1,-1),(0,0),(1,1). Shift 1 right, 2 down: inflection (1,-2); through (2,-1),(0,-3); root at x = 1+cuberoot(2) approx 2.26. Standard figure (p132 set).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.3 Ex 3.1 Q7(c); book p129 = PDF p156 (image read)

questions.knowledgeNote: y -> -y flips top-bottom: roots stay, the hump at (1/2,1/4) becomes a dip at (1/2,-1/4).
questions.question: Q7(d). Sketch y = x - x^2 and hence draw y = -(x-x^2) = -x + x^2.
questions.solution: Base: roots (0,0),(1,0), vertex (1/2,1/4) (maximum). Reflect in the x-axis: roots unchanged, vertex (1/2,-1/4) (minimum): y = -x+x^2. Cross-checked against the printed figure (p132): (0,0),(1,0),(1/2,...) and y = -2 marker consistent.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.3 Ex 3.1 Q7(d); book p129 = PDF p156 (image read); figure p132 verified

questions.knowledgeNote: Discriminant 1-8 < 0: no real roots - the whole parabola floats above the x-axis, lowest at (1/2,7/4).
questions.question: Q8(a). Sketch y = x^2 - x + 2.
questions.solution: y = (x-1/2)^2 + 7/4: vertex (1/2,7/4) (minimum); y-intercept (0,2); discriminant (-1)^2-8 = -7 < 0 so no x-intercepts. Cross-checked against the printed figure (p132): vertex (1/2,7/4) labelled with y = x^2-x+2.
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.3 Ex 3.1 Q8(a); book p129 = PDF p156 (image read); figure p132 verified

questions.knowledgeNote: One real root near x = 1.7 (f(1) = -3, f(2) = 3): down-left to up-right with two turning points.
questions.question: Q8(b). Sketch y = x^3 - x - 3.
questions.solution: y-intercept (0,-3); f(1) = -3, f(2) = 3 so one real root in (1,2) (approx 1.67); f'(x) = 3x^2-1: local max at x = -1/sqrt(3) (y approx -2.61), local min at x = 1/sqrt(3) (y approx -3.39); as x -> -inf, y -> -inf; as x -> +inf, y -> +inf. Standard figure (p132 set).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.3 Ex 3.1 Q8(b); book p129 = PDF p156 (image read)
